title: Trade Routes of the Eastern Mediterranean
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Predict five route-based outcomes, then see four simplified Eastern Mediterranean trade routes drawn across 16 ports and chokepoints.

educational.topic: Trade Routes of the Eastern Mediterranean
learningObjectives: Infer why places on chokepoints and sea lanes became rich or fought over, by predicting the outcome of five route-based questions before each route is revealed, scoring at least 4 of 5.
prerequisites: Bronze Age, Classical, Hellenistic, and Byzantine periods

keyQuestions: Where did most of the Uluburun ship's copper come from?
Which places must a grain ship from the Black Sea pass to reach Athens?
Why did Athens surrender after Aegospotami?
Why did Rhodes go to war with Byzantium in 220 BCE?
Why did Venice want Crete after 1204?
commonMisconceptions: Ancient trade went overland as much as by sea.
Wars were fought only over land and religion, not over sea passages.
Crete mattered to Venice only for its farmland.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on the five prediction questions (mastery: 4 of 5).
Name the places that appear on routes from more than one era.
